problem: Practical perception-aware visual navigation typically needs a prior precise metric map, while learning-based visual navigation needs large-scale training to generalize. Both hurt reliability.
motivation: Autonomous mobile robots need reliable visual navigation without costly precise metric maps or heavy training. Object-level topological semantic representations are lightweight, and semantic associations between objects can guide navigation.
key_idea: Build a lightweight object-level topological semantic map with graph memory, search it heuristically for a global path, split that path into segments using active perception and object guidance, and smooth the segments with Bernstein polynomial trajectory optimization.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablations can be cited. The abstract suggests that object-level topology removes the need for a metric map, and that path segmentation reduces cumulative error.
method: Object-level topological semantic map: a lightweight graph memory stores semantic associations between objects and organizes them topologically, in place of a precise metric map.
Object-based heuristic graph search: selects a global topological path that is optimal and shortest.
Global path segmentation: divides the global path using active visual perception and object guidance, to reduce cumulative error.
Bernstein polynomial smooth trajectory refinement: casts trajectory generation as a nonlinear planning problem, giving smooth multi-segment continuous navigation.
